la:other:Sulla.gloss: a cognomen used by the gens Cornelia
senses: a cognomen used by the gens Cornelia
la:other:Sulla.html:
Sulla (less correctly Sylla), ae, m.,
a surname in the gens Cornelia. So, esp.,
L. Cornelius Sulla Felix, the celebrated Roman dictator, ; ; ; .—Hence, Sullānus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Sulla: tempus,: ager,: assignationes,: proscriptio,: saeculum,: partes,: tempora,. — Subst.: Sullāni, ōrum, m., partisans of Sulla, .—
L. Cornelius Sulla Faustus, usually called Faustus Sulla, a son of the dictator, ; ; —
P. Cornelius Sulla, a relation of the dictator, accused of ambitus, and defended by Cicero in an oration still extant. —
Publius and Servius Sulla, conspirators with Catiline, ; cf. .—
An astrologer of the time of Caligula, .

la:verb:sullaturio.gloss: to (desire to) play or imitate the behaviour of Sulla
senses: to (desire to) play or imitate the behaviour of Sulla
la:verb:sullaturio.html:
sullātŭrĭo, īre,
v. desid. n. [Sulla], to imitate or play the part of Sulla: ita sullaturit animus ejus et proscripturit,; cf. ; .

la:adj:Sulpicius.gloss: of or pertaining to the gens Sulpicia.
senses: of or pertaining to the gens Sulpicia.
la:adj:Sulpicius.html:
Sulpĭcĭus, i, m.; Sulpĭcĭa, ae, f.,
the name of a Roman gens; e. g.
Ser. Sulpicius Galba, consul 610 A.U.C., and an able orator, ; .—
C. Sulpicius Gallus, a connoisseur in Greek literature, and a good orator, ; ; .—
Ser. Sulpicius Rufus, a very celebrated jurist, a contemporary and correspondent of Cicero; v. sqq.; ; —
C. Sulpicius Apollinaris, a grammarian, teacher of the emperor Pertinax, ; .—
A tribune of the people. author of the lex Sulpicia, ; . —
Sulpicia, a Roman poetess in the time of Domitian, ; .—Hence,
Sulpĭcĭus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to a Sulpicius: horrea,: lex, proposed by the people's tribune P.Sulpicius, .—
Sul-pĭcĭānus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to a Sulpicius: classis, commanded by the prætor P. Sulpicius, : seditio, raised by P. Sulpicius, .

la:noun:sulcus.gloss: A furrow made by a plow.
senses: A furrow made by a plow.
A long, narrow trench; a ditch.
la:noun:sulcus.html:
sulcus, i, m.
Gr. ὁλκός, from ἕλκω
,
a furrow made by the plough (cf.: lira, porca): sulci appellantur, quā aratrum ducitur, vel sationis faciendae causā vel urbis condendae, vel fossura rectis lateribus, ubi arbores serantur: quod vocabulum quidam ex Graeco fictum, quia illi dicant ὁλκόν, Müll.: quā aratrum vomere lacunam striam facit, sulcus vocatur: quod est inter duos sulcos elata terra, dicitur

porca, : sulco vario ne ares,: cum sulcus altius esset impressus,: ducere ... infodere sulcum,; : duci sarculo sulcum,: proscindere jugerum sulco,: sulco tenui arare,: sulcum patefacere aratro,: sulcis committere semina,: mandare hordea sulcis,: telluri infindere sulcos,: semina longis Cerealia sulcis Obruere,: herba Cerealibus obruta sulcis,.—

Transf. (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
A ploughing: hordeum altero sulco seminari debet,: quarto,: quinto,: nono,.—
Of things resembling a furrow.
A long, narrow trench, a ditch, ; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.—
A rut, track, in gen.: cursu rotarum saucia clarescunt nubila sulco, Claud. Cons. Prob. et Olymp. 102.—Esp., of the furrow cut by a vessel: infindunt sulcos,: delere sulcos,: canebant aequora sulco,.—Of a wrinkle of the skin, : genarum,.—Of the trail of a meteor, ; .—Of wounds: in pectore,.—Of the private parts of a woman, ; ; App. Ἀνεχ. 16.

senses: to sail over, traverse, pass through, cross
la:verb:sulco.html:
sulco, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
sulcus
,
to furrow, cut furrows through, to plough (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; not in Cic. or Cæs.).
Lit., in agriculture: agros,: (rura) sulcata Camilli Vomere,: vomere humum,: campos vomere,. — Absol.: recto plenoque sulcare,.—
Transf.
Ingen., to furrow, plough;poet., to sail over, traverse, pass through, etc.: sulcant fossas, quo pluvia aqua delabatur,: (anguis) harenam Sulcat,: iter caudā,: longā sulcant vada salsa carinā,: rate undas,; : maria arbore,: regna volatu,: sulcavitque cutem rugis,furrowed her skin with wrinkles,: gressus,: sulcatis lateribus,i. e. by lashes,.—
To elaborate, to work out (cf. exaro), Ven. Fort. Vita Mart.

sulfŭrĕus (sulph-), a, um, adj.
id.
,
of or like sulphur, sulphurous, sulphureous: fornaces,: aqua,: lux fulminum,: color,: odor,.
